I now have a complete picture of the implementation. I've reviewed the backend (models, API, search parser/tokenizer, enrichment, snapshot, archive.org, import/export, markdown, URL normalization) and the frontend (list/detail/add/views/import-export/preferences pages and components). Let me assess each requirement.

Key findings:
- **All core CRUD, search, tags, read-later, bulk, sort** are fully realized in code.
- **Search grammar** (tokenizer + recursive-descent parser) supports `#tag`, AND/OR/NOT, parens, quoted phrases (operators inside quotes treated literally), case-insensitive LIKE.
- **Duplicate handling** via `normalizeUrl` + `url_key UNIQUE`, POST returns `duplicate` with `existingId`, frontend routes to existing bookmark.
- **Snapshot** produces self-contained single HTML with inlined assets; PDF sources detected (content-type or `.pdf`) and stored as PDF.
- **Archive vs delete**, archived-only view, archive.org save, markdown notes, saved views (query+include/exclude tags), Netscape import/export (title/tags/date), preferences (sort/items/font) — all implemented.
- **REF-BM-03 nuance**: title/description are fully editable *after* saving, and the create API accepts overrides, but the Add flow only takes a URL and enriches asynchronously — there is no pre-save preview/edit of the auto-collected metadata. The "before saving" facet is not realized in the UI/behaviour.
